notes.decision: Translated 'branch' (of a river). The term recurs lines 1, 8, 28 always with ⲡⲓⲉⲣⲟ 'river' or ⲛ̄ⲛⲥⲧⲟⲓⲭⲉⲓⲟⲛ 'of the elements,' confirming the watercourse-tributary sense (cf. Coptic ⲧⲱⲧ as 'joining/fork' or ⲧⲟⲩⲱⲧ 'channel'). Preserves the hydrographic register central to the chapter's punitive-river vision.
Rendered 'great river of Judgment.' ⲧⲓⲕⲣⲓⲥ = Greek κρίσις with prosthetic ⲧⲓ-. Capitalized as cosmic principle: this is the underworld punitive river that pours fire into the mouths of bound archons.

Translated 'down' (toward the archons' mouths). ⲁϩⲣⲏⲓ̈ in Lycopolitan/Sahidic can denote either upward or downward; the punitive context (river pouring into mouths to burn) requires the downward reading. The bound archons are 'upon the land of Death' (line 20), so the river descends to them.

Translated 'they continually burn them' — ϣⲁ- habitual + ⲣⲁⲭϩ (Lyc. = ⲣⲱⲕϩ̄ 'burn,' cf. ⲣⲱⲭⲍ̄ in vocabulary) + 3pl object. The verb pairs with ⲣⲱⲭϩ̄ 'his burning' in line 5, confirming the burning-judgment register.
Translated 'marvel/wonder.' Lyc. ⲣⲱⲡⲏⲣⲉ = ϣⲡⲏⲣⲉ 'wonder, marvel.' Recurs lines 11, 14, 29 — the elect one's marveling response to the apostle's revelation about the river of Judgment.

Translated 'prison' rather than 'destruction.' In context with 'mighty boundary' and the bound/blackened/buried archons (line 18), the carceral sense fits. Cf. ⲡⲩⲧⲉⲕⲟ 'the prison' in accumulated vocabulary.

Four-fold passive/qualitative chain: 'they are bound (ⲭⲁⲗⲭ = ϫⲱⲗϫ̄), they are fettered (ⲙⲏⲣ qual.), they are blackened (ⲕⲙⲕⲁⲙⲧ̄ reduplicated of ⲕⲙⲟⲙ), they are buried (ⲧⲁⲙⲥ̄ = ⲧⲱⲙⲥ̄).' Each represents a discrete mode of archonic captivity in correspondential register.

Translated 'foundation/support' per accumulated vocabulary. Recurs lines 25, 29, 32 in 'foundation of the lions / of the man / of the First Man' — the cosmic-anthropological support upon which the archonic punishment-system rests.

Read as 'this little one now, the rivers being reckoned' — ⲡⲓⲕⲟⲩⲓ 'this little one' (small) + †ⲛⲟⲩ 'now' + ⲛⲓⲉⲣⲟ ⲏⲡ 'the rivers being counted.' The contrast between the diminutive earthly river and the cosmic river of Judgment (line 26: 'one out of a thousand') structures the passage.

notes.coptic_form: ⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲉⲣⲟ ⲅⲁⲣ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲱⲧ ϩⲛ̄ ϣⲟ ⲛ̄ⲗⲉⲣⲟ
notes.decision: 'For one river out of a thousand rivers' — ϣⲟ = 'thousand' (Coptic ϣⲟ). The exegetical formula contrasts the visible earthly river with the hidden cosmic-judicial multitude.

Tentatively read 'this multitude' (ⲡⲓ- + ⲁϣⲁⲓ̈ 'be many' + -ⲡⲉ copula). Context (god whose power holds the lions/archons) supports a quantitative-greatness term. Alternative reading 'this disgrace' (ⲡⲓ-ⲁϣⲓⲡⲉ from ϣⲓⲡⲉ 'shame') would yield 'this great disgrace within the power' — possible but less coherent with 'How great is that god.' Confidence low.
Translated 'the one which is exalted' — qualitative ⲟⲩⲁⲧⲃⲉ 'be exalted/lifted up' (cf. accumulated vocabulary). Modifies the troubled voice of wrath, contrasted (line 24) with thunders.
